---
title: "Week 10: Gun Violence Prevention: Fatal and Nonfatal Injury Patterns,
Tree Equity, and Policy"
---

## Theme

Gun violence is not random. It clusters in corridors shaped by
disinvestment, concentrated poverty, lack of greenspace, and the same
historical redlining patterns examined in Week 2. This week we use
Chicago\'s publicly available fatal and nonfatal shooting dataset ---
one of the most detailed open-source urban violence databases in the
country --- to map violence patterns, examine environmental predictors
including tree equity, and connect the spatial analysis to Public
Nuisance Law and environmental accountability frameworks.

**Assignment 3 Check-In:** Assignment 3 is due tonight. Your 2-page

## Classroom Lab Demonstration

**Legal Focus:** Public Nuisance Law and holding property owners legally
responsible for environmental conditions that facilitate violence;
Justice40 Initiative mandating equitable distribution of federal
environmental investment; Second Amendment jurisprudence and the limits
of gun violence research funding under the Dickey Amendment.

**Health Focus:** Fatal and nonfatal firearm injuries as a public health
epidemic; the distinction between homicides and nonfatal shootings in
surveillance (nonfatal data is systematically undercounted); the
environmental health argument that urban tree canopy deficits create
heat islands that are associated with increased violence.

**Data:** Chicago Violence Reduction --- Victims of Homicides and
Non-Fatal Shootings dataset (City of Chicago Data Portal:
data.cityofchicago.org/Public-Safety/Violence-Reduction-Victims-of-Homicides-and-Non-Fa/gumc-mgzr/about_data
--- direct download as CSV, updated regularly, free); Tree Equity Score
(American Forests, treeequityscore.org); Chicago community area
boundaries (City of Chicago Data Portal); HOLC shapefiles for Chicago
(dsl.richmond.edu/panorama/redlining).

**R Code:** read_csv() for Chicago violence data; lubridate::mdy() to
parse dates; dplyr::group_by(community_area) + summarise(n()) to
aggregate by area; sf::st_as_sf(coords=c(\'longitude\',\'latitude\'),
crs=4326) to convert point data; sf::st_join() for spatial join to
community area polygons; ggplot2 geom_sf() choropleth; geom_point() for
dot density map of individual incidents.

- Download Chicago Violence Reduction --- Victims of Homicides and
  Non-Fatal Shootings data from the City of Chicago Data Portal
  (data.cityofchicago.org/Public-Safety/Violence-Reduction-Victims-of-Homicides-and-Non-Fa/gumc-mgzr/about_data);
  load in R

- Convert latitude/longitude columns to sf spatial object using
  st_as_sf(); set CRS to EPSG:4326; transform to Illinois State Plane
  projection (EPSG:26971) for accurate area calculations

- Aggregate shooting incidents to Chicago community area using
  sf::st_join() and dplyr::count(); compute incident rate per 10,000
  population using 2020 Census population data

- Produce a choropleth map of shooting incident rates by community area;
  overlay HOLC grade boundaries to examine the redlining-violence
  relationship

- Load Tree Equity Score data for Chicago (treeequityscore.org); join to
  community areas; produce a bivariate map of violence rate vs. tree
  equity score using biscale
